candidates.summary: isCrossingCurParam dropped the realm-type test, so any body-level name `cur` in a crossing function with an unnamed first realm parameter is refused, including an int local that compiled and ran on the merge base
candidates.failure_scenario: In a realm: `func F(_ realm) int { cur := 1; cur = 2; return cur }` — the `_ realm` shape is used by r/gnoland/blog, r/gnoland/boards2/v0, r/demo/counter, r/sys/users and others, so the function has no `cur` parameter at all. The body-level `cur` is declared by the crossing FuncDecl's own block, and the rewritten write rule keys on name plus declaring node with the old `evalStaticTypeOf(store, last, ne) == gRealmType` gate removed, so preprocess panics at the DEFINE with "cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter". The same file compiles and prints 2 on the merge base, where DEFINE was skipped wholesale and ASSIGN required the realm type. The `&cur` arm carries the same hole: its message still says "realm-typed `cur`" while nothing checks the type.

candidates.summary: the FuncDecl/FuncLitExpr arms test IsCrossing() alone, so a named result `cur` in a crossing function whose first realm parameter is unnamed is refused, against the godoc's "a named result ... stays writable"
candidates.failure_scenario: `func F(_ realm) (cur realm) { cur = nil; return cur }` in a realm: IsCrossing() only asks whether Params[0].Type == gRealmType, and the FuncTypeExpr naming rule lets that parameter be unnamed (`.arg` prefix), so a `cur` that is a named result resolves to the same crossing FuncDecl and the write is refused with a message naming a parameter the function does not have. This predates the branch (it fails on the merge base too), but the branch sweeps exactly this class — its godoc, the PR body's fix 2 and the new zrealm_cur_other_legal.gno all state that a named result stays writable — and misses this member. Adding `&& ft.Params[0].Name == "cur"` to both arms closes it.

candidates.summary: the legal-shapes filetest's namedResult is non-crossing, so it pins nothing about the named-result claim its header makes and stays green while the crossing shape is refused
candidates.failure_scenario: The header says a package-level var, a named result and a block-scoped local "keep compiling" because they are not a crossing parameter, but `func namedResult(x int) (cur realm)` has an int first parameter, so isCrossingCurParam returns false at the first hop (the declaring node is a non-crossing FuncDecl) and the write rule never resolves anything. The shape the claim is about — a named result in a function the declaration test calls crossing — is `func F(_ realm) (cur realm)`, and it panics. The fixture therefore certifies a rule the code does not implement, and would stay green through a fix or a further regression.

candidates.summary: the provenance arms test IsCrossing() alone too, so a named result `cur` is accepted as a frame identity at preprocess and rejected at runtime under the stale-capture wording, which names a mistake the source did not make
candidates.failure_scenario: `func F(_ realm) (cur realm) { Target(cur); return }` with `func Target(cur realm)` in the same realm: the cur-call check resolves `cur` to the crossing FuncDecl, accepts it, and the value forwarded is the result's zero realm. installInheritedCur then panics with "a stale capture from another frame, a sibling frame, or a rebound cur" and the remedy "pass the caller's own `cur` unchanged", neither of which describes writing `Target(cur)` inside a function whose `cur` is a result. Fail-closed and pre-existing, so the cost is a wrong diagnosis; the same `Params[0].Name == "cur"` test that closes the write rule turns it into the existing preprocess error.

candidates.summary: the rewritten header's "a fresh allocation that never matches" holds only for prevs that are PointerValues; NewConcreteRealm and MakeRealmValue plant gOriginRealmTV itself as the prev field whenever the prev argument is not one
candidates.failure_scenario: curUsesPreprocessOrigin reads Fields[2] and compares its HeapItemValue to originPlaceholderHIV(). Both realm constructors start from `prevField := gOriginRealmTV` and only replace it when `prev.V.(PointerValue)` holds with a non-nil TV, so any realm minted with a nil or non-pointer prev carries the one global placeholder as its prev and answers the predicate true. A cur that answers true is rebuilt from buildOriginRealm and, through `rebuilt`, is exempted from the caller-identity check below — the fail-open the header says identity comparison closed. MakeRealmValue is the testing stdlib's own constructor (X_makeRealm), so the reachable surface today is test-only; the claim as written is what a later caller would rely on.

candidates.evidence: Read only: uverse.go:461 and uverse.go:474 both open with `prevField := gOriginRealmTV`; buildOriginRealm (uverse.go:415) returns newRealmHIVPointer(m.Alloc, addr, pkgPath, TypedValue{}), whose own Fields[2].V is nil, so the materialized origin itself is correctly not matched — the gap is one hop up, in what is stored as another realm's prev.
